author: nflaig
content:
I don't think lodestar is really affected by removing the signature, we only verified it during gossip validation and import, the payload root check should replace this without any issues

dropping the signature should be mostly relevant for clients that checked it before knowing the block, since in that case you cannot check the payload root, but either way, that signature check is easy to abuse since you just need a few builders or validators to work around it

author: raxhvl
content: Wouldn't that block out an honest envelope if any peer just sends about 5 junk envelope to loadstar today?

author: nflaig
content:
possibly, but we request the envelope by root later. the point is that the signature doesn't really help a lot here, you need cap the queue one way or the other, for us it's 2 per root, to prevent dos. it's trivial for an attacker to get enough keys to exhaust the queues even if we verify the signatures

but the point is we queue by beacon block root, so an attacker would have to learn about the beacon block, and fill our queue before the node itself learns about the beacon block and at the same time it can only happen in scenarios in which the proposer (or builder) broadcast the payload really early. it does happen on devnets (or kurtosis) that we receive the payload first, but that seems mostly a symptom of small networks

could probably make it more robust by adopting some ideas from https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/1570462426657202188/1572443650418409554

but irrespective of that, I don't see how the signature would buy us anything

author: raxhvl
content:
agree that signature doesn't meaningfully fix the underlying squatting problem just limits to peers with keys that hardly improves security.

imo signature removal is forcing us to revisit these false assurances, hopefully that improves overall security
